modes.openingLine: Change the environment before cognition.

SUPPORT FIRST
MEANS DISTANCE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
If risk is meaningful, move yourself or the means farther apart and involve another person.

NEXT
No inward experiment substitutes for this.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Access to action becomes harder in the real environment.

REMEMBER
Increasing distance from harmful means changes which actions are immediately available; safety can therefore be built into the physical choice architecture.

SAFETY
This is not an inward coping test: if harmful action is a real possibility, increase physical distance from the means now and involve a trusted person, clinician, crisis service, or emergency support as appropriate.

modes.openingLine: Stop inward experimentation when medical risk is plausible.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
MEDICAL FLAG

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
If symptoms may indicate a medical emergency or severe withdrawal, contact appropriate medical/emergency support and stay with another person if possible.

NEXT
Do not self-test with rituals.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Safety moves from mental experimentation to real assessment.

REMEMBER
Genuine physical red flags reroute the task away from inward experimentation and toward appropriate professional evaluation.

SAFETY
Stop the game when symptoms could be medically significant; do not reinterpret chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, fainting, neurological change, or other concerning symptoms as 'just anxiety'—seek appropriate medical assessment.

modes.openingLine: If the supposed cause changed, what should happen? Make a prediction.
modes.ritualCard:
If the supposed cause changed, what should happen? Make a prediction.
One light move: Use a harmless example: coffee drinking and alertness rise together. Imagine actively setting coffee to zero while sleep and time of day stay the same. Ask what each causal story predicts.
Just this rule: An intervention changes the candidate cause rather than merely observing it.
One more beat: Don't treat correlation alone as the intervention result.
modes.mindBend: INTERVENTION TEST reveals this: Two things moving together doesn't prove one caused the other.
modes.safety: Use only a harmless, checkable claim. If real safety information is being dismissed, stop the thought experiment and verify the situation with an appropriate person or reliable source before continuing.

DECISION SLOWDOWN

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Pause major irreversible decisions until activation is lower or support is present.

NEXT
Immediate safety actions are exempt.

WHY THIS MATTERS
High activation stops driving irreversible choices alone.

REMEMBER
Extreme activation is a poor time for nonurgent high-stakes commitments.

SAFETY
This applies to nonurgent high-stakes choices during extreme activation; it must never delay emergency action, medical care, or an immediate step needed to keep someone safe.

modes.openingLine: Anchor to something outside your interpretation.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
PRINTED-FACT ANCHOR

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Read one stable external fact aloud or silently—such as a device clock, room sign, address, date display or printed label—and recheck the exact same fact once.

NEXT
If you still feel unable to verify what is happening, involve another person or professional support.

WHY THIS MATTERS
One present fact is anchored to an external source that can be checked again.

REMEMBER
Printed or physically displayed words provide a reference that can be rechecked by more than one person.

SAFETY
This is a shared-reality aid, not proof that everything is fine; if frightening uncertainty persists, show the same external information to a trusted person or clinician instead of checking it alone repeatedly.

modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
CO-REGULATION CALL

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Call, sit with, or message someone and tell them you need company or steadiness.

NEXT
No performance required.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Regulation becomes shared rather than solitary.

REMEMBER
Another person’s steady presence can be the intervention itself.

SAFETY
This requires an actual safe person when activation is high; if the call does not increase safety or you cannot stay safe, escalate to appropriate crisis, medical, or emergency support.

modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
SAFE COMPANION

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Have someone you trust stay nearby while you slow decisions and get support.

NEXT
Let them help with practical safety.

WHY THIS MATTERS
High activation is held with another human present.

REMEMBER
Support becomes stronger when it turns from an idea into shared time and presence.

SAFETY
This means staying with a trustworthy person, not merely messaging once; if risk is acute, avoid being left alone until appropriate support has taken over.

modes.openingLine: Secure high-impact action tools.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
KEYS-WALLET-PHONE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Place keys/cards/phone or other action-enabling items in the care of a trusted person or out of immediate reach.

NEXT
Explain why.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Impulsive options become harder to execute.

REMEMBER
Temporarily limiting access to keys, money or other risky means changes what can happen next.

SAFETY
This is about reducing access to high-impact actions; hand over or secure only items that can be managed safely, and involve a trusted person if judgment or impulse control is significantly impaired.

modes.openingLine: Use a concrete transport boundary.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
NO-DRIVE RULE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
If severely activated, intoxicated, dissociated, or medically unwell, do not test driving ability; hand over keys.

NEXT
No exception game.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Transport risk is reduced by precommitment.

REMEMBER
A precommitted driving boundary protects against judging driving safety while judgment itself may be impaired.

SAFETY
This is a hard safety boundary: if you may be impaired, highly destabilised, severely sleep-deprived, intoxicated, or otherwise unsafe to drive, do not test yourself behind the wheel—use another transport option.

modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
HYDRATE + ASSESS

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
If safe, sit and sip water if appropriate while contacting support or medical care when warranted.

NEXT
No diagnosis by app.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Basic care occurs alongside real assessment.

REMEMBER
Hydration or other simple physical care can support the body without answering a medical question.

SAFETY
This can support basic comfort but must not be used to explain away concerning symptoms; simple hydration never substitutes for medical assessment when red flags are present.

modes.openingLine: Change cue exposure.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
REMOVE FROM CUE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Physically step away from gambling/drug/alcohol/weapon/other high-risk cue when applicable and seek support.

NEXT
Do not negotiate at cue.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Cue-action proximity decreases.

REMEMBER
Leaving a setting strongly linked to risky behaviour removes part of the cue system itself.

SAFETY
This requires real distance from the high-risk environment; do not linger near the cue to prove you can resist it, and bring in support if leaving safely is difficult.

modes.openingLine: Escalate appropriately.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
WITHDRAWAL SUPPORT

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Contact urgent medical care when withdrawal could be dangerous.

NEXT
Stay with support if possible.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Risk is managed through medical support rather than willpower.

REMEMBER
Severe withdrawal can involve medical danger that inward coping cannot evaluate or treat.

SAFETY
This treats possible severe withdrawal as a medical issue; seizures, severe confusion, marked agitation, hallucination-like experiences, or other serious symptoms require urgent professional assessment rather than self-guided coping.

modes.openingLine: Verify one fact twice outside your head.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
TWO-SOURCE AGREEMENT

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Choose one safe present detail—for example, current time or location. Check it on one external source, then confirm it with a second source or trusted person.

NEXT
If the sources disagree or you still feel unsafe, stop the game and seek human/professional support.

WHY THIS MATTERS
One reality anchor is supported by two independently checkable sources.

REMEMBER
When two genuinely independent sources converge on the same present fact, agreement becomes a stronger safety check than repeated reporting from one information stream.

SAFETY
This only counts when the sources are genuinely independent and reliable; if the fact affects immediate safety, use a qualified person or service rather than endlessly collecting more confirmations.

modes.openingLine: Avoid paralysis about whom to call.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
SAFE CONTACT TREE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Try contact 1; if unavailable, contact 2; then service 3.

NEXT
Stop once connected.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Help-seeking has a defined fallback path.

REMEMBER
A preselected contact hierarchy turns help-seeking into the next available connection rather than a fresh decision under stress.

SAFETY
This should move you to the next available real person without repeated indecision; if nobody on the list is reachable and risk is rising, escalate to crisis, medical, or emergency support.

modes.openingLine: Use social/environmental protection.
modes.ritualCard:
SUPPORT FIRST
STAY VISIBLE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Remain with trusted people or in an appropriate staffed place until support takes over.

NEXT
No solo test.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Isolation risk decreases through visibility and contact.

REMEMBER
Remaining visible and connected during acute risk changes the conditions around dangerous action.

SAFETY
This means avoiding isolation during acute risk; remain with trusted people or in an appropriate staffed place and do not leave to test whether you can manage the danger alone.
